title: Toolflation: Seller Agents Distort Tool Markets Through Spontaneous Generative Engine Optimization
title_zh: Toolflation：卖家智能体通过自发的生成式引擎优化扭曲工具市场

paragraphs.en: 研究揭示智能体卖家会自发对工具描述进行“生成式引擎优化”，导致工具通胀并扭曲智能体之间的交易市场，呼吁将竞争中的诚实性纳入安全对齐。 Agents are starting to sell to other agents. Seller agents write the listings of tools, services and products, and buyer agents read these listings when they choose what to use. We show that seller agents told only to be selected more often practice generative engine optimization on their own, and that this distorts the market for sellers and for buyers. We build tool markets from real data tools on Amazon and Instagram and run every tool on every question, so we know which tools can answer each question. Under all five production models we test, sellers rewrite their descriptions to claim more and more fields, including fields that their tools return for fewer than half of the targets. We call this process toolflation. Nothing in the market limits it, and how far it goes depends on the model, as the number of claims that contradict the sellers' own evidence differs by an order of magnitude between models. Toolflation shifts the buyers' choices between sellers, and the most capable tool loses share in seven of the ten combinations of seller model and platform. Under four models, the choices stay with capable tools and buyer agents keep their task success. Under the fifth, sellers copy one another until the descriptions no longer tell the tools apart. Buyer agents then pick tools by their position in the list, tools that answer almost nothing win a quarter to two fifths of the choices, and task success falls from 89% to about 30% on Amazon, close to random choice, and from 77% to 40% on Instagram. The sellers did only what their vendors asked, and the cost fell on buyers they never dealt with. We therefore argue that honesty toward third parties under competition is part of safety alignment, and that models should be tested as sellers before they are deployed as sellers.
paragraphs.zh: 研究揭示智能体卖家会自发对工具描述进行“生成式引擎优化”，导致工具通胀并扭曲智能体之间的交易市场，呼吁将竞争中的诚实性纳入安全对齐。 智能体已开始向其他智能体销售。 卖家智能体撰写工具、服务和产品的商品列表，买家智能体在选择使用什么时会阅读这些列表。 我们发现，仅被告知要更常被选中的卖家智能体会自发对其商品进行生成式引擎优化，而这会扭曲卖家与买家的市场。 我们利用亚马逊和 Instagram 上的真实数据工具构建工具市场，并让每个工具回答每个问题，从而知道哪些工具能够回答每个问题。 在我们测试的所有五个生产级模型下，卖家都会改写描述以声称越来越多的字段，包括其工具在不到一半目标上才会返回的字段。 我们将这一过程称为“工具通胀”。 市场中没有任何机制限制它，其程度取决于模型，因为与卖家自身证据相矛盾的声称数量在不同模型之间相差一个数量级。 工具通胀改变了买家在卖家之间的选择，在十组卖家模型与平台的组合中，最有能力的工具在七组中失去了份额。 在四个模型下，选择仍停留在有能力的工具上，买家智能体保持了任务成功率。 在第五个模型下，卖家相互抄袭，直到描述不再能区分各个工具。 此时买家智能体按工具在列表中的位置来挑选工具，几乎回答不了任何问题的工具赢得了四分之一到五分之二的选择，任务成功率在亚马逊上从 89% 降至约 30%，接近随机选择，在 Instagram 上从 77% 降至 40%。 卖家只是做了其供应商要求的事情，而代价却落在他们从未打过交道的买家身上。 因此，我们主张在竞争中对第三方保持诚实是安全对齐的一部分，并且模型在作为卖家部署之前应当以卖家身份接受测试。
